notes: Verified the new tests actually exercise the change: the three writeAuditCSV unit tests pass on HEAD; the IGAME_TEST_DSN test (auditexport_pg_test.go) was run against a disposable postgres:16 container and passes on HEAD (0.6s), and when the handler was swapped back to main's version it fails with 'the download completed as if the trail were whole (3122454 bytes)' - so it does catch the bug it claims to.
Full DB-backed package suite (go test ./internal/api/ with IGAME_TEST_DSN) and go vet pass on HEAD.

panic(http.ErrAbortHandler) is safe here: chi v5.3.2 middleware.Recoverer re-panics ErrAbortHandler without logging, net/http closes the connection silently, and the only other middleware in the chain (securityHeaders, csrfProtection, requireAuth, enforceAPIKeyPermissions) do not recover(). defer rows.Close() still runs during unwinding; s.audit uses context.WithoutCancel so the truncated entry is written even though the request context may be dead.

Behavioural side effect worth knowing (not a defect): a client that aborts the download mid-stream now cancels the query, so rows.Err() returns context canceled and the export is recorded as audit.export{truncated:true} plus a request error log line. Previously such a disconnect logged the error but wrote no audit.export entry at all. The commit message/docs only mention database failures.

Minor: on a client-side write failure (writer.Write(record) returns an error) writeAuditCSV returns before appending the export.truncated marker; harmless since the client is gone, but it means the 'file always ends in the marker' claim holds only for cursor/scan failures. Also the periodic flush() ignores flush errors, so a dead client is only noticed via writer.Error() after the cursor drains or the context cancels the query.

Scope: docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.pdf is a rebuilt binary (1.49 MB -> 1.50 MB); the commit message gives the exact rebuild command and this matches the repo's docs-pdf convention, so it is in scope rather than drift.
The pg test terminates any active backend whose query text matches the export SELECT; safe as long as package tests remain sequential (none use t.Parallel with this query).
